result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A supplier without an agreed value gets 30. The full offline suite passes (176 test classes, no failures), including the new test.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)`.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component, plus a `STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30` constant. A 5-argument constructor defaults to 30, so the existing call sites in tests and `DemoScenario` still compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms, so renegotiating is just an update with the new value.
  - The four listings you named (by name, by country, by minimum rating) and `findSupplierById` read the column.
  - I also updated the other queries that build a `Supplier` (purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance, spending per supplier and category-to-single-supplier). Without this they would have shown the 30-day default for every supplier.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: new `paymentTermsAreShownInAllListingsAndAfterRenegotiation` test. It registers a supplier at 45 days, renegotiates it to 14, checks all four listings and the lookup show 14, and checks a supplier registered without terms shows 30.

Nothing is committed.
